summary: This is the opening section of Thomas Hoover's novel Life Blood, narrated by Morgan Smyth James, a 38-year-old single filmmaker driving to a location shoot that is meant to wrap principal photography on her first feature, Baby Love, a film about the pain and joy of adoption. Reflecting on her life, she regrets not having the family she once planned, explaining that at 20 she turned down two suitors to focus on her film career and developed a habit of boxing up heartbreak and denying it. The excerpt ends as she begins describing a change in her feelings from three years earlier.
one_line: Opening of Thomas Hoover's novel Life Blood, following filmmaker Morgan Smyth James on the set of her first feature while reflecting on her single life.
key_facts: The novel excerpt is titled 'Life Blood' by Thomas Hoover and is labeled 'Book 3 — part 1'.
The story opens in New York, New York on a cloudless spring morning as the narrator drives her high-mileage Toyota down Seventh Avenue.
The narrator, Morgan Smyth James, is thirty-eight, single, and strives to be eternally optimistic.
Morgan Smyth James is named after two grandmothers.
Morgan is headed to a location shoot meant to wind up principal photography for her first feature film, Baby Love.
Baby Love is a film about the pain and joy of adoption.
Morgan is missing a man named Steve terribly on the morning of the drive.
Eighteen years before the narrative present, just out of college, Morgan turned down two really nice guys.
Morgan's greatest fear in her early twenties was getting 'trapped' into motherhood, while her grad school plans loomed.
Morgan met a director named Jason at NYU film school, and he dumped her for his undergraduate sweetheart who had gotten pregnant during his Christmas break.
After the breakup, Morgan developed a fallback strategy: she put all heartbreak in a special box, nailed down the lid, and acted as though it wasn't there.
Morgan decided to focus her life on learning to make movies and let the family part play out naturally, reasoning that a career could be controlled while men's affections could not.
Morgan admits she lives in selective denial, a habit she says makes her a survivor.
The excerpt ends with the narrator noting that three years back, she had started lingering, leaving the thought unfinished.
